scope: KTX2 worker lifecycle and recovery only. Parent owns startup/resource/main and final full-suite/build/deployment.

confirmedMechanisms.name: SDK worker initialization rejection poisons a single-worker pool
confirmedMechanisms.result: Original and explicit retry remained pending; rejected worker slot stayed non-idle and queued action could not run.

confirmedMechanisms.name: SDK returns an errored worker to idle without health recovery
confirmedMechanisms.result: A fatal/no-response worker boundary was reused; explicit retry could remain pending.

changes: Single worker supervisor reuses the official SDK applyConfig/workerFunction/initializeWebWorker; no decoder/transcoder or SDK source copy is deployed.
Failed initialization, worker/channel errors and total-await timeout terminate that exact worker, settle queued jobs, and latch failure. Failed jobs are never retried automatically.
The next explicit map setup/manual retry invokes initializeVillageKtx2 and recovers the latch; a fresh worker is created only when a new decode request arrives.

Final InternalTexture owner release cancels only its active/queued decode. Shared references survive. Same-turn cancellation is coalesced before pumping, so 20 old queued owners cause zero replacement-worker churn.
Healthy queue is serial and copied only at dispatch; existing caps, decoder options, compressed format, mipmaps and output option metadata remain intact.
Owner metadata is a non-enumerable Symbol on a private options copy and is excluded from cache keys and worker message options.
Engine disposal and stale worker completion cannot retain an active slot, publish a decoded result or install a texture into a newer map.
Existing external/native pools and workerless runtimes are preserved and explicitly identified in diagnostics.
Root failure stage/detail is preserved separately from errors of jobs waiting in the queue; successful manual recovery marks the historical failure recovered.
Before invoking SDK initialization in its scheduled microtask, verify the same live lease/job; same-turn cancellation cannot attach late init listeners to an already terminated worker.

actualCodecCase.workerSimulation: official SDK worker script in isolated VM, not a browser/physical worker/GPU

verification.focusedLogScope: 44/44 before the final one-guard same-turn init-listener correction; final supervisor suite then passed 12/12. Parent executes the complete suite after this source lock.

limitations: These deterministic SDK failure mechanisms are reachable, but no new user-device trace proves which one caused a specific reported failed journey.

No browser automation, actual browser worker scheduler, GPU timing or phone temperature measurement. The codec comparison runs the official worker source and shipped JavaScript/WASM in an isolated VM.
The 45-second ceiling is total decode wait including queue and worker initialization. A legitimately slower first 8K decode can also hit this ceiling; queue/init/active timing is reported separately.
A timeout callback cannot preempt synchronous JavaScript/WASM execution before the event loop runs. Worker termination stops that owned worker; it does not cancel unrelated normal/shared textures.

If an external/native pool was already registered before installation, it is preserved rather than silently taking ownership; inspect reports external-pool and this supervisor does not claim to repair that foreign pool.
